instruction.text: Find London on this map of the British Isles.

feedback.end: London was the place worst affected by the Great Plague, which broke out in 1665. A plague is a very dangerous illness that spreads quickly.
In 1665, most people were suffering from a specific type of plague called the bubonic plague.

instruction.text: To understand more about the bubonic plague, let’s ask an expert. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: How was the ((++bubonic gigantic)) plague spread?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.5st'>How was the bubonic plague spread?</prosody>

atoms.b: The bubonic plague was spread by ((++fleas unicorns)) that lived on rats.
atoms.sound: ssml: The bubonic plague was spread by fleas that lived on rats.

atoms.b: How did it make people feel?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.5st'>How did it make people feel?</prosody>

atoms.b: When someone was bitten, they would suffer from headaches, a ((++fever smile)) and swellings called buboes.
atoms.sound: ssml: When someone was bitten, they would suffer from headaches, a fever, and swellings called <phoneme alphabet='ipa' ph='ˈbjuːbəʊs'>buboes</phoneme>.

instruction.text: Did the bubonic plague cause these things?
Drag King Charles II to the countryside.

feedback.finish: King Charles and the rest of the rich people in London fled to the countryside to avoid the plague, but this just helped to spread the plague even further!

instruction.text: Flea-infested parcels sent across the country also spread the plague. Select the cloth to learn more about the village of Eyam.

feedback.finish: Eyam is a village in Derbyshire that was very badly affected by the plague. It was most likely spread to them by cloth that had fleas on it. Historians think 80% of Eyam’s population died because of the outbreak.

instruction.text: Listen and choose the correct statement.

b.sound: The plague spread very quickly around the country.
The plague didn’t spread at all.

feedback.finish: Overall, the plague killed nearly 70,000 people in London and thousands more across England.
